story.headline: Oil Is the Headline. The Real Yield Is the Bill.

question: Can the AI trade survive a 10-year Treasury above 5% and an oil shock at the same time?

call.stance: The trade pays the real yield
call.line: Oil reaches the AI trade through the Fed and the real yield while inflation expectations stay put. The multiple shrinks; the trade survives.
actions: Split every move in the 10-year into real yield and breakeven: from Feb 27 to Oct 8, 2026, 115 of its 125 basis points were real.
Price long-dated earnings against a 10-year at 5.5%, where Howell's Aug 14 projection put the market multiple below 20 times.
Count AI borrowing as a rates input: Eisman tied about $500 billion of AI debt issuance to the 10-year's climb on Oct 9.
flips: The 10-year closes at 5.50% or higher with breakeven inflation under its May 4 high of 2.50%: the two shocks compound.
The 5-year, 5-year forward rate on FRED closes above 2.60%: the shock has reached inflation expectations.
The Fed holds on October 28 and the real yield closes under 2.50% by December 9: the boom is paying the rate.

nextTest.event: The 10-year: whether FRED's daily series closes at 5.50% or higher on any business day from October 16 through December 31, 2026, after a 5.31% high on October 5.

resolver.rule: Read every daily observation of DGS10 dated October 16, 2026 through December 31, 2026, as FRED shows them on January 5, 2027; the days read are the days for which FRED reports a value. The answer is yes if any of them is 5.50 or higher; no if every one is below 5.50. Intraday highs, other maturities and yields reported in the press are read alongside and do not decide the test.
resolver.question: Does the 10-year Treasury constant-maturity yield (FRED series DGS10) close at 5.50% or higher on any day from October 16, 2026 through December 31, 2026 for which FRED reports a value?

source.label: FRED, Market Yield on U.S. Treasury Securities at 10-Year Constant Maturity (DGS10), Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System

resolver.ambiguity: FRED posts each close about one business day later, so the observation for December 31, 2026 is due by January 4, 2027. A weekday FRED leaves blank because the U.S. bond market was closed is not missing and is not read: in this window, Veterans Day (November 11), Thanksgiving (November 26) and Christmas (December 25, 2026), by the holiday schedule of the Securities Industry and Financial Markets Association. Only a weekday on which the bond market was open and FRED still shows no value on January 8, 2027 is missing; if one is, and no observation already in is 5.50 or higher, the test is inconclusive, and the Result says what was read and what was missing; the next reading is January 15, 2027. A close FRED revises before the reading is read as revised; a later revision does not reopen the test.

settles.event: The 10-year: whether FRED's daily series closes at 5.50% or higher on any business day from October 16 through December 31, 2026, after a 5.31% high on October 5.
The barrel: whether the EIA's January outlook puts Brent's fourth-quarter 2026 average above the $105 a barrel it forecast on October 6, 2026.
Expectations: whether FRED's 5-year, 5-year forward inflation rate averages above 2.60% in March 2027, from 2.32% on October 9, 2026.
The trade: whether the Thrift Savings Plan's C Fund, an S&P 500 index fund, closes 10% or more below its highest close since October 16, 2026, on any day through March 31, 2027.
